data.title: yuki.sato@sunrise.test is missing DMARC
data.group_title: {count} sending domains are missing authentication records
data.detail: The sending domain for yuki.sato@sunrise.test has no valid DMARC record. Google's bulk sender rules require SPF, DKIM, and DMARC to be aligned, so unauthenticated cold mail is filtered on arrival regardless of how good the copy is.
data.remedy: Add the missing DNS records at the domain's registrar, then re-check the domain from the mailbox to clear it immediately. This is the highest-leverage deliverability fix available and it costs nothing.
steps: Open your DNS provider for the domain this mailbox sends from. The records to add are below, ready to paste.
Add the DMARC record as a TXT record at the _dmarc host. It starts at p=none, which monitors without affecting delivery; tighten it to quarantine once a few weeks of reports look clean.
Give DNS up to a few hours to propagate. Most providers are much faster.
Send yourself a test message and check the headers show a pass for each record. Warmbly re-checks the domain on its own schedule and this clears itself once it does.

data.title: 3 contacts who unsubscribed are still in Sunrise Q3 launch outreach
data.group_title: {count} campaigns still have unsubscribed contacts enrolled
data.detail: 3 contacts in Sunrise Q3 launch outreach have unsubscribed but are still enrolled. Mailing someone who opted out is the fastest way to earn a spam complaint, and in several jurisdictions it is not merely impolite.
data.remedy: Remove them from the campaign. If they are still receiving mail, that is a routing problem worth understanding before anything else in this campaign.
steps: Open the campaign's contacts and filter to unsubscribed.
Remove them from the campaign. Suppression stops future sends, but leaving them enrolled keeps the campaign reporting an audience it must not mail.
Check whether any of them were sent to after they unsubscribed. If so, stop the campaign: that is a routing problem, and every further send compounds it.
Check where the list came from. Unsubscribed contacts reappearing usually means a re-import overwrote their status.

data.title: liam.walsh@sunrise.test is bouncing 4.5% of its sends
data.group_title: {count} mailboxes are bouncing too much mail
data.detail: 72 of 1599 sends from liam.walsh@sunrise.test bounced in the last 30 days. Amazon SES asks senders to stay under 5% and can pause sending at 10%; mailbox providers read a high bounce rate as a sender who does not know who they are mailing.
data.remedy: This is a list problem, not a mailbox problem. Verify the contacts in the campaigns this mailbox sends for before sending more, and remove the domains that bounce repeatedly.
steps: Pause the campaigns this mailbox sends for, so the rate stops climbing while you work.
Open Contacts and filter to the lists those campaigns use.
Run verification on the list, or re-import it from a verified source.
Delete or suppress every address that hard-bounced. Those never come back.
Resume sending, and watch the bounce rate on this page for a few days before raising volume again.

data.title: Opener reads like bulk mail
data.group_title: {count} steps read like bulk mail
data.detail: Opener uses "act now", "congratulations", "double your", "free trial", "guarantee", "limited time", "no obligation", "no strings attached", "once in a lifetime", "risk free", "this is not spam" and "100% free". Filters weight these phrases, but the bigger cost is that they make the message read as something nobody wrote to anyone in particular.
data.remedy: Rewrite those lines in the words you would use in a one-to-one email to this person. If a phrase would be strange to say out loud, it is strange to read.

data.title: Opener has copy that will not render
data.group_title: {count} steps have copy that will not render
data.detail: The body and plain-text body in Opener cannot be parsed as a template (line 1: unexpected EOF). Sending does not fail on this: it falls back to plain replacement, so conditionals and merge variables go out to the recipient as literal text.
data.remedy: Fix the template syntax. Check that every {{if}} has a matching {{end}}, that quotes are balanced, and that field names have no stray characters.
steps: Open the campaign and go to Opener.
The parser stopped here: line 1: unexpected EOF.
Every {{if}} and {{range}} needs its own {{end}}. A missing {{end}} is the most common cause and the error usually points past it, not at it.
Write a field with a leading dot, like {{.FirstName}}; the first_name and firstName spellings of built-in fields work too. A custom field is {{.city}}, or {{index . "city"}}.
Save, then use the preview to check it renders against a real contact rather than trusting that it looks right.

data.title: 25.0% of Q4 outbound (first draft) is shared inboxes
data.group_title: {count} campaigns are mailing mostly shared inboxes
data.detail: 25.0% of the 160 contacts in Q4 outbound (first draft) are addresses like info@ or sales@. Shared inboxes rarely reply, are usually read by someone with no interest in the offer, and complain at a higher rate than a named recipient does.
data.remedy: Filter role addresses out of the list and find the named person instead. A smaller list of real people outperforms a larger one of shared inboxes on every metric that matters.

data.title: The first email in Q4 outbound (first draft) has 4 links
data.group_title: {count} first emails carry too many links
data.detail: Opener carries 4 links in a first-touch email. Filters treat link-heavy first contact as a bulk signal, and a reader with four things to click does none of them.
data.remedy: Keep one link, or none. The goal of a first email is a reply, not a click.

data.title: The subject line in Opener is stacked with exclamation marks
data.group_title: {count} subject lines shout
data.detail: The subject "DON'T MISS OUT!! Our LIMITED TIME offer for your team is closing soon!!" is stacked with exclamation marks. Filters weight this as a bulk-mail marker, and a person reads it as shouting from a stranger.
data.remedy: Write it the way you would write to one person: sentence case, no exclamation marks.
